message.content:
**Answer:** The most iconic sculpture of the 19th century is generally considered to be **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by Auguste Rodin, created in 1889. **Why it’s so famous** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin – one of the most influential sculptors of the late‑19th century. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast), with subsequent editions produced throughout the 1890s. | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend; it captures the intimate, almost tactile moment between lovers. | | **Technique** | Bronze casting on a stone base; the work shows Rodin’s mastery of surface texture and anatomical detail. | | **Cultural Impact** | • It became a symbol of modern romanticism.
• Its copies and reproductions spread worldwide, making it one of the most widely recognized sculptures.
• It influenced later artists such as Picasso and Matisse. | | **Legacy** | • The original is housed at the Musée Rodin in Paris.
• Numerous casts exist in major museums (Metropolitan Museum of Art, National Gallery of Art, etc.). | **Contextual note** While “The Thinker” (1902) is often cited as Rodin’s masterpiece, “The Kiss” predates it by over a decade and remains the quintessential 19th‑century sculpture in terms of public recognition and influence.
